Freeze the reviewed contract before generation. Required is a task decision, not
an intrinsic property of an example. Each criterion ID is stable within this
rubric and references the source RQ it evaluates. Scope changes create a new
rubric version; keep the old version and reevaluate every compared candidate.

## Required and optional behavior checks

| Criterion ID / source RQ | Required? | Setup, state and viewport | Action | Expected observable result | Evidence method/location | Failure severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | | | | | | |

Record each result as pass, fail or unverified. Specify interaction checks that
require a running candidate. Screenshots alone cannot verify those interactions.
These task checks do not establish comprehensive accessibility conformance.

## Subjective criteria and anchors

| Criterion ID / source RQ | Required? / task threshold | What serves this brief | 1: major shortcomings | 3: meets criterion with evidence | 4: exceeds criterion usefully | Evidence method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | | | | | | |

Proposed scale: 0 contradicts the criterion; 1 major shortcomings; 2 partial; 3 meets;
4 exceeds in service of the brief. Supply criterion-specific examples for 1/3/4;
the generic scale does not calibrate taste. Missing observation is unverified,
not 0. Existing brand reuse can meet or exceed a criterion; novelty is not required.
Record thresholds explicitly; minimum 3 is only a proposed starter choice.

## Selection and stopping

Required behavior must pass, required rated criteria must meet their reviewed
thresholds and required evidence must exist before contract acceptance. Optional
scores can compare eligible candidates only; they cannot compensate for a failure
or missing evidence. No default weighted total is required.

Record contract-satisfied, budget-exhausted, plateau or unresolved-decision as the
stop reason. Stopping is distinct from acceptance: needs-work when no candidate
qualifies. Compare candidates only with matching rubric versions and evidence.
Human overrides record the decision and residual risk; they do not relabel failed
checks, invent evidence or bypass repository finish gates.
